post.caption: A Roman bulla was a gold bubble. Bulla is Latin for bubble, and the pendant looked like one. Free born Roman children, mainly boys, wore it on a necklace. Wealthy families used gold, and poorer ones used leather. Each hollow pendant held a lucky charm. Girls wore a similar charm shaped like a crescent, the lunula. Romans likely borrowed the custom from the Etruscans. Etruscan gold bullae survive from at least the 5th century BC. Around age 14, a boy gave his bulla to the household gods. The bull in papal bull comes from bulla, meaning a seal.
